script.title: Why Builders Dragged Stonehenge 150 Miles from Wales
sentences: Parts of Stonehenge were hauled across one hundred and fifty miles.
Around 2600 BC, builders raised dozens of two-ton bluestones on Salisbury Plain.
Geologists traced these specific rocks straight to the Preseli Hills in Wales.
Scientists initially assumed natural glaciers pushed the boulders east.
Then archaeologists found prehistoric quarry cuts right in the Welsh mountainside.
Nearby, an older Welsh stone circle had been dismantled around the exact same period.
Migrants had actually uprooted their sacred Welsh monument and moved it across Britain.
Why haul eighty massive stones across the country just to rebuild them?
script.description: Stonehenge's bluestones didn't come from anywhere near Wiltshire. Archaeologists revealed they were dragged over 150 miles from prehistoric Wales.
visuals: Waun Mawn stone circle Preseli Hills Wales
claims_en: Stonehenge is located on Salisbury Plain in England.
Around 2600 BC, builders installed bluestones weighing about two tons each.
The bluestones originated in the Preseli Hills in Pembrokeshire, Wales, about 150 miles away.
Glacial transport was once theorized to have brought the rocks closer.
Evidence of megalithic quarrying proved the Welsh stones were excavated by humans.
An identical 110-meter stone circle was dismantled at Waun Mawn in Wales around the same era.
Archaeologists suggest migrants dismantled the Welsh circle and relocated the stones to Stonehenge.
Stonehenge held up to 80 standing bluestones in its double ring phase.
